name: Canyoning in der Wolfsschlucht
beschreibung:
Abseiling, jumping, sliding and wading through crystal-clear Alpine water – canyoning is one of the most thrilling outdoor adventures in the Tyrolean mountains. The Stubaital itself offers spectacular nature trails along wild mountain streams (WildeWasserWeg, Burkhardsklamm), while guided canyoning tours head to the established gorge areas of the neighbouring Inn Valley and Ötztal.

Tours & Offers

Sport Stubai in Neustift (Stubaitalstraße 62) organises guided canyoning tours to Tyrol's best-known gorges, including the Alpenrosenklamm, Rosengartenschlucht near Imst and the more challenging Auerklamm in the Ötztal (approx. 45–60 min from Stubaital).

Beginner canyoning (e.g. Alpenrosenklamm): difficulty Level 1–2, minimum age 10–12, total guided tour duration approx. 3.5–5 hours. Price: approx. €75–95 per person incl. equipment and certified guide.

Advanced tours (e.g. lower Auerklamm): Level 3, jumps up to 10 m, abseils up to 40 m. Minimum age: 16–18. Price: approx. €110–145 per person. Season: approx. 1 May to 15 October.

Important: Commercial canyoning tours in Tyrol may only be led by state-certified guides (Tiroler Bergsportführergesetz). Never enter unknown gorges independently!

Getting There

Booking: Sport Stubai KG, Stubaitalstraße 62, 6167 Neustift im Stubaital, Tel. +43 5226 30288. By public transport: Stubaitalbahn (STB) from Innsbruck to Neustift/Fulpmes.
